- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.7) and forecast shows a sharp upward spike, reduce the peak by 5–10% to avoid overshoot.  
- If sentiment is negative (≤ -0.3) and forecast is overly conservative, slightly increase the early-period lows to reflect mean reversion.  
- For 30-day forecasts, if the last 3–5 days of history show a clear downward trend, the model tends to overcorrect — adjust forecast downward by 2–5% in the first 10 days.  
- When sentiment is volatile (alternating ±0.3–0.5), avoid smooth extrapolation — introduce a 1–2 day lag in the forecast’s peak or trough to match sentiment momentum.  
- If the model consistently overpredicts early in the forecast horizon (first 7–10 days), apply a 3–5% downward bias to the first 5 days of the forecast.  
- For sentiment history with high positive momentum (e.g., 0.8+ for 3+ days), model often overestimates — apply a 5–8% downward correction to the 10–15 day forecast window.
